people.name: Kavya Mehta
people.wants: A growth story the board can believe.
people.fear: Discovering the headline was bought with cash.

people.name: Omar Reyes
people.wants: A weekly forecast he can defend.
people.fear: Running out of cash before the next round.

people.name: Dani Kwon
people.wants: Keep the customers who actually stay.
people.fear: Being blamed for a system everyone celebrated.

people.name: Tomas Aranda
people.wants: Keep written promises to neighborhood businesses.
people.fear: Real partners being treated as fraud.

people.name: Rhea Shah
people.wants: An announcement she can answer questions about.
people.fear: A screenshot proving the company said two things.

people.name: Priya Nand
people.wants: Evidence of a sustainable referral model.
people.fear: Funding incentives rather than product value.

lines.speaker: kavya
lines.text: Six weeks. Five times the users. Tonight, take a moment. You built this.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: I saved you a drink. Though Omar has been staring at that spreadsheet all night.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: The stage says one hundred twenty thousand in weekly payouts. My ledger says four hundred ten thousand.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Before anyone calls this sustainable, help me explain the difference.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Ana refers Ben. Ben refers Ana back. What should that pair earn? Try it here.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: You own referrals at Gilt, a neighborhood marketplace. I'm Omar, your finance partner.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: I'm Dani. I run growth. We celebrated signups before checking who stayed.

lines.speaker: kavya
lines.text: I'm Kavya, the CEO. We have twelve weeks of cash. Find the real growth worth keeping.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Three evidence pulls tonight. Then set payouts, protect useful customers, and explain the change.

lines.speaker: kavya
lines.text: The board wants a sentence from you. Can we keep this growth going?

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Pick three reports. Each costs one pull. Opened reports stay in your case file.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Try devices, purchases, and location. Separate fake accounts from people who really buy here.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: These controls change weekly payouts. Watch runway, then commit a week to see the result.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: The signup curve moved. I need to know which customers we lost, not just how many.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Exactly. Cheaper growth means little if we cut the customers who create value.

lines.speaker: kavya
lines.text: People are asking if mutual referrals are a feature. What can we honestly promise tonight?

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: I'm Tomas. I work with the neighborhood Guilds. Those gold loops are actual shops.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Leena's bakery sends customers to the florist. They send people back. Both make sales.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: We put mutual referral bonuses in their contracts. She hired someone against that income.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Please separate the fake accounts from the promise we made her.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Assign a policy to each segment. The forecast includes lost Guild revenue, not just saved rewards.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Notice buys people time, but costs cash. Thirty days honors the month we promised.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: I called it a flywheel in the board deck. I should have looked past the curve.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Let's keep what works. I can live with a smaller number if it's real.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: I'm Rhea, community lead. Give me a reason, timing, exceptions, and somewhere people can ask questions.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: Someone posted our old message beside today's plan. Read both before you answer.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: Reviews are falling. People feel the rules changed underneath them. We need to own that.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: There's pushback, but people understand the change. Matching our words to the rollout helped.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I'm Priya, your lead investor. We can bridge two million dollars for eight percent ownership.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: That buys time. It doesn't fix the referral model. The dilution is permanent.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: We have enough runway to avoid an emergency bridge. Keep measuring the customers we retained.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: We have one recovery team this week. Community support, partner repair, or a tighter cash forecast?

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Splitting it helps both teams a little. Pick what you can actually stand behind.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Here's the ledger. What you kept, what you cut, and what it cost. Start with the conclusion.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: One phone, fourteen accounts, no purchases. That's a fraud signal, not a neighborhood business.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: The gold loops buy again without a bonus. That's the difference I missed.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Three neighborhoods. Different phones. These are businesses sending customers to each other.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Account age alone doesn't separate these groups. We spent a check, but learned no useful pattern.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: There it is. The stage left out circular rewards. The missing cost is two hundred ninety thousand.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Some rings are huge. Others are just two shops. We can't call them all the same thing.

lines.speaker: dani
lines.text: Guild customers are worth four times the average. Cutting that loop would cut real value.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Fourteen accounts on one phone. Start there, before touching the shops buying every week.

lines.speaker: rhea
lines.text: People built routines around these rewards. They'll want a reason, not just a switch turning off.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: That's our signature. Mutual referrals qualify. We need to handle this as a promise we made.

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: Twelve weeks sounds comfortable until you need to raise money. The clock is already running.
